text: The Git object store keeps blob, tree, commit, and tag objects under .git/objects; a blob holds file content, a tree maps names to blobs, and a commit points at one tree plus its parents.

queries.text: what four object kinds live under the Git object directory and how do they relate
git object store blob tree commit tag .git/objects

text: We switched the mirror from loose objects to packfiles because a million loose files were exhausting inodes on ext4; `git repack -ad` now rolls the repo into a single .pack plus its .idx.

queries.text: why did the mirror move to packfiles and which command rolls the repo into one
git pack loose object inode ext4 repack idx mirror

text: Delta compression in a Git packfile stores an object as an offset plus a diff against a base object; the window of candidate bases is set by `pack.window` and the search depth by `pack.depth`.

queries.text: how does a packfile shrink object size and which two config knobs govern base selection
git delta compression pack window depth base object diff

text: refs/heads, refs/tags, and refs/remotes form the three main namespaces under .git/refs; `git pack-refs` collapses them into packed-refs to cut directory churn on repos with thousands of branches.

queries.text: which three ref namespaces does Git expose and how does pack-refs help repos with many branches
refs heads tags remotes packed-refs pack-refs namespace

text: The reflog at .git/logs/HEAD saved us after a bad rebase: `git reflog` showed the pre-rebase tip and `git reset --hard HEAD@{4}` restored the branch without touching anyone else's clone.

queries.text: how did the reflog rescue a branch after a bad rebase and which reset flag completed the recovery
git reflog reset hard HEAD rebase rescue recover

text: Git garbage collection only prunes objects unreachable from any ref or reflog entry; setting `gc.reflogExpireUnreachable` shorter is what finally let `git gc --prune=now` actually drop the leaked blobs.

queries.text: why did git gc refuse to drop leaked blobs and which reflog expiry setting unblocked it
git gc prune reachability reflog expire unreachable leak

text: HEAD is normally a symbolic ref pointing at a branch under refs/heads; a detached HEAD happens when you check out a commit directly, and new commits land on no branch until you name one.

queries.text: what does HEAD normally point at and what does detached HEAD mean for new commits
head symbolic ref detached branch checkout commit orphan

text: Rebase rewrites the branch by replaying commits on a new base, while merge preserves history with a merge commit; we standardised on rebase for feature branches and merge for release integration.

queries.text: how did we split rebase and merge across branch roles in the standard workflow
git rebase merge feature branch release integration workflow

text: Standardised on cherry-pick with `git cherry-pick -x` for porting security fixes from main to maintenance branches; the -x flag records the source SHA in the body so the audit trail survives.

queries.text: which cherry-pick flag did the team pick for porting security fixes and what audit trail does it leave
git cherry pick security fix maintenance branch source sha audit

text: The kitchen corkboard collected nine postcards from the same coastline before anyone noticed the pattern.
Interactive rebase via `git rebase -i HEAD~8` lets you squash, fixup, reword, or drop commits before pushing; fixup is the quiet cousin of squash that discards the marked commit's message.

queries.text: which actions does interactive rebase offer and how does fixup differ from squash
git rebase interactive squash fixup reword drop commit

text: `git reset --soft` keeps the index and working tree while rewinding HEAD, `--mixed` resets the index too, and `--hard` discards local changes; the soft variant is the rewrite-my-last-commit move.

queries.text: what do the three git reset modes each preserve or discard and which rewrites the last commit
git reset soft mixed hard index working tree rewind

text: Reflog rescue after `git reset --hard`: the lost commits sit under HEAD@{n} entries for the configured expiry (90 days by default), so a fresh branch at the right reflog slot recovers the work.

queries.text: how long does the reflog hold commits lost to a hard reset and how do you bring them back
reflog rescue reset hard head at n 90 day expiry branch

text: We replaced the Git submodule layout with a git subtree because contributors kept forgetting `git submodule update --init --recursive`; subtree bakes the dependency into the super-repo history instead.

queries.text: which Git embedding strategy replaced submodules and what contributor friction drove the swap
git submodule subtree super repo update init recursive

text: `git worktree add ../hotfix release-2026.03` let the on-call engineer patch production without stashing the feature work in the main checkout; each worktree has its own index and HEAD.

queries.text: which Git mechanism gave the pager-duty responder a second checkout for a release-line patch without disturbing feature work
git worktree add hotfix release index head parallel checkout

text: Sparse-checkout with cone mode trims the working tree to the directories you actually touch; `git sparse-checkout set services/api libs/core` cut the checkout from 42 GB to 3 GB for the monorepo hires.

queries.text: how did sparse-checkout shrink the working tree and which cone mode command drove the cut
git sparse checkout cone mode monorepo trim working tree size

text: Partial clone with `git clone --filter=blob:none` (the blobless variant) fetches commits and trees but defers blobs until checkout touches them; treeless (`--filter=tree:0`) goes further and defers trees too.

queries.text: how do blobless and treeless partial clones differ in what they defer fetching
git partial clone filter blob none tree zero defer fetch

text: `git bundle create snapshot.bundle --all` produced an offline transfer artefact for the air-gapped build farm; the remote side runs `git clone snapshot.bundle` and fetches incrementally from it afterwards.

queries.text: how does git bundle move a repository into an air-gapped environment for the build farm
git bundle create all air gapped build farm offline transfer

text: Signed commits moved from GPG to SSH signing with `gpg.format = ssh`; allowed-signers files replaced the GnuPG keyring and CI verifies every tag with `git verify-tag` before release.

queries.text: why did we swap GPG signing for SSH and how does CI check tags before a release
git signed commit gpg ssh format allowed signers verify tag

text: Sigstore's gitsign lets developers sign commits with their OIDC identity and a short-lived certificate from Fulcio; no local key material and no keyring rotation to manage across the team.

queries.text: how does gitsign sign commits without local keys and which Sigstore service issues the certificate
sigstore gitsign oidc fulcio short lived certificate key less

text: pre-commit hooks run locally before a commit is recorded; commit-msg hooks validate the message after; pre-push hooks gate the push itself. We use all three via the pre-commit framework.

queries.text: which three Git hook stages fire around commit and push and how do we orchestrate them
git hook pre commit message push framework stage orchestrate

text: .gitignore patterns are glob-based with directory anchoring via leading slash and negation via leading bang; trailing-slash patterns match directories only, which fixed the stray file/dir ambiguity.

queries.text: how does a .gitignore pattern anchor to directories and express negation
gitignore glob pattern leading slash bang negation directory

text: .gitattributes drives merge drivers, text/binary treatment, linguist language detection, and LFS filter routing; the `* text=auto eol=lf` line is what finally tamed the Windows CRLF churn.

queries.text: which behaviours does .gitattributes control and which incantation fixed the Windows line-ending churn
gitattributes merge driver linguist lfs text auto eol lf crlf

text: I keep rerere enabled globally via `rerere.enabled=true` on every dev machine; the conflict-replay win on any long-running integration rebase is worth the minor hygiene of clearing stale resolutions.

queries.text: why do I leave rerere enabled globally on every dev machine despite the stale-resolution hygiene cost
git rerere enabled global dev conflict replay rebase hygiene

text: `git bisect start HEAD v4.2` plus `git bisect run ./repro.sh` narrowed a perf regression to a single commit in nine steps; the script exited non-zero on the bad tick-rate measurement.

queries.text: how did git bisect run automate pinpointing the performance regression commit
git bisect start run repro perf regression nine step automate

text: filter-branch is deprecated in favour of git-filter-repo by Elijah Newren; filter-repo is faster, safer about refs, and doesn't choke on the forty-thousand-commit history the old tool timed out on.

queries.text: which tool replaced filter-branch for history rewriting and who authored the successor
git filter branch repo elijah newren deprecate history rewrite

text: Chose `git filter-repo --replace-text secrets.txt` as the standard history-scrub playbook for any leaked AWS key incident, paired with a same-hour force-push to every mirror and a key rotation.

queries.text: how did we purge leaked AWS keys from the repo history and what mitigations ran alongside the rewrite
filter repo replace text aws key purge history rotate force

text: Git LFS hosts the heavy assets — PSDs, FBX, and game-ready meshes — while the pointer files stay in Git; `git lfs track '*.psd'` set the clean/smudge filter that swaps blobs at checkout.

queries.text: how does Git LFS split heavy assets from the main repo and which filter swaps blobs at checkout
git lfs pointer clean smudge filter track psd large asset

text: We picked Nx over Lerna for the TypeScript monorepo; Nx's affected-graph scheduling and remote cache shaved CI from 24 minutes to 4, and Lerna's publish flow was already showing its age.

queries.text: which monorepo tool replaced Lerna for the TypeScript workspace and what CI win justified it
nx lerna typescript monorepo affected graph remote cache ci

text: Turborepo's pipeline config declares task dependencies and remote caching targets; `turbo run build --filter=web...` rebuilds only the web package and its downstream consumers, not the entire graph.

queries.text: how does Turborepo restrict rebuilds to one package and its downstream consumers
turborepo pipeline filter web downstream cache rebuild task

text: Bazel won the polyglot-monorepo bake-off against Pants v2; hermetic toolchains and remote execution scaled past a thousand targets where Pants's Python-first runtime started to stall.

queries.text: why did Bazel beat Pants for the polyglot monorepo and which scaling property mattered most
bazel pants hermetic toolchain remote execution polyglot monorepo

text: GitHub's branch protection rule on main requires signed commits, a passing CI check, two approving reviews, and a linear history; the last constraint rejects merge commits from the UI merge button.

queries.text: which four gates does the GitHub branch protection rule on main enforce
github branch protection main signed commit review linear history

text: Adopted GitLab's `workflow:rules` block to gate merge-request pipeline starts in detached pipeline mode; the alternative of keeping both branch and MR pipelines active was the duplicate-pipeline trap.

queries.text: which GitLab config gate stopped the duplicate pipeline storm on every merge-request push
gitlab ci merge request detached pipeline workflow rules gate

text: Migrated the internal mirror from Gitea to Forgejo after the fork diverged; federation support and the community governance model lined up better with the open-infra policy.

queries.text: why did the internal mirror migrate from Gitea to Forgejo after the fork
gitea forgejo fork federation governance mirror migrate

text: Bitbucket's default-reviewer rule auto-assigned the platform team to every pull request touching infrastructure/; we used that with CODEOWNERS-style gates to keep unowned changes from sneaking in.

queries.text: how did Bitbucket's default-reviewer rule keep unowned infrastructure changes from slipping through
bitbucket default reviewer pull request codeowners infrastructure

text: I default to a shallow clone via `git clone --depth 1` on every CI image build and deepen with `git fetch --unshallow` only when a git-describe tag is needed; shaved two minutes off every pipeline and the trade-off is rarely felt.

queries.text: how did shallow clone speed up CI and which command restores the full history later
git shallow clone depth one fetch unshallow ci describe tag

text: Commit SHA-1 collisions remain implausible in practice, but Git's transition to SHA-256 objects is tracked under the `objectformat` extension; we kept SHA-1 until the tooling ecosystem catches up.

queries.text: which hash function will replace SHA-1 for Git objects and why did we stay on SHA-1 for now
git sha1 sha256 object format extension hash collision tooling

text: `git maintenance start` schedules background prefetch, commit-graph, and incremental-repack tasks via systemd timers on Linux; pull time on the 3 GB repo dropped from 40 s to 6 s after a week of runs.

queries.text: which background Git maintenance tasks cut pull time on the 3 GB repo and how are they scheduled
git maintenance start prefetch commit graph incremental repack systemd

text: The commit-graph file at .git/objects/info/commit-graph caches parent and generation-number info so `git log --graph` and merge-base queries skip walking the object store for every call.

commit graph info generation number log merge base cache parent

text: Multi-pack index (`git multi-pack-index write`) indexes all packs at once so object lookups stop linearly scanning a dozen .idx files; turned on automatically once maintenance is enabled.

queries.text: which index replaces scanning many .idx files and when does maintenance enable it by default
git multi pack index write idx scan maintenance enable lookup

text: Reachability bitmaps accelerate clone and fetch by precomputing the set of objects reachable from each pack's tip; `pack.writeBitmaps = true` pays off on any server-side repo with many fetchers.

queries.text: which packfile index speeds up clone and fetch on busy server-side repos
git reachability bitmap pack write clone fetch server tip

text: `git switch` and `git restore` split the overloaded `git checkout` into branch ops and file ops; onboarding docs now teach the new pair by default since the semantics are no longer context-guessed.

queries.text: which two commands split the overloaded git checkout and why do the onboarding docs teach them now
git switch restore checkout split branch file onboarding teach

text: Someone swapped the break-room mug with an identical twin again and there's an ongoing investigation involving a fingerprint kit.

git pull rebase autostash feature branch style guide merge clutter

text: `core.fsmonitor` hooked into Watchman so `git status` on the 200k-file monorepo went from 7 s to 200 ms; Git asks Watchman for the changed-file set instead of stat-ing every tracked path.

gitlab protected tag signed push impersonation force refuse deploy

github codeowners pull request terraform branch protection enforce

git notes add refs notes builds provenance release commit opt in

commit graph multi pack reachability bitmap sre playbook mirror cpu

github gitea git push mirror cron runner pat alert route
